title: Ibrance (palbociclib): Product Science — Mechanism, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, Formulation, Metabolism, and Drug Interactions
summary: Ibrance (palbociclib) is an orally administered, selective small-molecule inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6), approved by FDA in 2015 and indicated for HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an aromatase inhibitor, fulvestrant, or (as of a more recent label update) inavolisib plus fulvestrant. Per FDA-approved labeling (DailyMed/FDA prescribing information), palbociclib blocks CDK4/6-mediated phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma (Rb) protein, arresting susceptible tumor cells in G1 phase and reducing proliferation, with enhanced antiproliferative/senescence effects when combined with antiestrogens in vitro. Oral bioavailability is moderate (46%) and food intake reduces inter-subject exposure variability; the drug reaches steady state within 8 days, exhibits dose-proportional kinetics across the tested range, and has a mean elimination half-life of ~29 hours in patients with advanced breast cancer. Palbociclib is primarily metabolized by CYP3A and the sulfotransferase enzyme SULT2A1, with elimination predominantly fecal, and it is a weak time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, giving rise to clinically important interactions with strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers as well as sensitive CYP3A substrates. Available capsule and tablet formulations differ in food requirements (capsules require food; tablets can be taken with or without food). Hepatic and renal impairment affect exposure, with specific dose adjustments defined in labeling for severe hepatic impairment.

gaps: Exact plasma protein binding percentage for palbociclib and volume of distribution (Vd or Vd/F) were not directly captured from the label excerpts retrieved in this search; would need direct confirmation from full Section 12.3 PK text.

Full renal impairment pharmacokinetic data (mild/moderate/severe, dialysis) were not retrieved in complete form; only a truncated statement indicating dialysis-requiring patients have not been studied was found.
Specific inactive ingredients/excipients for capsule vs. tablet formulations (e.g., fillers, coating agents) were not retrieved from DailyMed in this research pass.

Peer-reviewed pharmacology papers characterizing the biochemical selectivity/potency (IC50) of palbociclib against CDK4/6 versus other kinases were not independently verified via PubMed in this search round; current claims rely on FDA label and label-derived tertiary sources (Pfizer Medical, Elicit, RxList) rather than original peer-reviewed enzymology papers.

The label's precise molecular mechanism section (12.1) was captured largely via Pfizer Medical patient-facing clinical pharmacology pages and DailyMed tablet label rather than the single canonical current FDA PDF; version differences between capsule/tablet labels and across approval supplements were noted but not fully reconciled (e.g., current fully updated label with inavolisib indication vs. earlier archived PDFs).
warnings: Some retrieved FDA label PDFs are explicitly marked as not reflecting the most current approved labeling (e.g., 2016 and 2019 archived PDFs), and label content has evolved with new indications (e.g., addition of inavolisib combination) and dosing information (e.g., tablet vs. capsule food requirements); claims here are cross-checked against multiple label versions/DailyMed setids but exact current live label should be reconfirmed at time of use.

Several source URLs (Pfizer Medical patient/HCP clinical pharmacology pages, RxList, fda.report, Elicit) are secondary/tertiary aggregator sites that reproduce label language; when possible these were cross-validated against DailyMed/FDA PDF text, but original canonical FDA label sourcing was not obtainable for every claim within the search budget.

No independent peer-reviewed pharmacology (e.g., PubMed primary kinase-selectivity or human ADME study) papers were directly retrieved and cited in this section; metabolism/ADME claims rely on FDA label text describing underlying human radiolabeled ADME study results rather than the primary published study report.

Clinical onset of pharmacodynamic effect (e.g., time to neutropenia nadir) was not addressed in this section per the instruction not to infer clinical onset from half-life; this would require separate clinical/safety data not covered by the current search scope.
